name: Tesla Powerwall 3
description: Tesla's 13.5kWh LFP home battery with an 11.5kW continuous rating and a built-in solar inverter, the benchmark for whole-home backup when you add solar.
quick: 13.5kWh LFP, 11.5kW, Built-In Solar Inverter. Tesla's 13.5kWh LFP home battery with an 11.5kW continuous rating and a built-in solar inverter, the benchmark for whole-home backup when you add solar.
skipIf: You want to buy and install a battery yourself
specs: 11.5kW, Built-In Solar Inverter, whole-home backup capable
Additional Powerwall 3 units or DC expansion packs (13.5 kWh each)
verdict: The Powerwall 3 is the benchmark installed home battery, and the strongest single unit here for whole-home backup. It is the best value when you are adding solar at the same time.

**Power is the standout.** Tesla rates it at 13.5 kWh of usable storage and 11.5 kW of continuous output. That continuous figure matters more than capacity during an outage: 11.5 kW at 240 volts is about 48 amps, enough in one unit to run most of a typical home, including many central air conditioners. The earlier [Powerwall 2](/gear/tesla-powerwall-2/) was rated at 5 kW continuous.

**How long it lasts.** 13.5 kWh at an average outage draw of 1.5 kW is about 9 hours; trimmed to essentials at 0.5 kW, about 27 hours. Solar recharges it each day, which is how battery-only homes ride out multi-day outages. The [power station runtime calculator](/tools/power-station-runtime-calculator/) works the same math on smaller units.

**Built-in solar inverter.** Unlike earlier models, it has a solar inverter built in, so a new solar-plus-storage system needs one less box, and DC expansion packs add 13.5 kWh at a time without another inverter. It uses [LFP](/glossary/lifepo4/) chemistry and carries a 10-year warranty.

Owners report seamless switchovers and like the app; the common complaints are installer wait times and quotes well into five figures. It is sold only through Tesla and certified installers. It leads our [home battery backup](/best-home-battery-backup/) guide.

Built-in solar inverter saves a box on new installs
DC expansion packs add 13.5 kWh each
Mature app and wide installer network
cons: Installer-only, so price is a local quote
Best value only alongside new solar
Installer wait times in busy markets

faqs.q: Can a Tesla Powerwall 3 run central air?
faqs.a: In many homes, yes. Its 11.5 kW continuous rating is about 48 amps at 240 volts, enough for a typical 3- to 4-ton central AC plus lighting and a fridge. Large or older AC units with high starting current may need a soft starter on the compressor. Your installer checks the AC against the battery when sizing the system.

faqs.q: How long will a Powerwall 3 power a house?
faqs.a: It depends on your load. With 13.5 kWh usable, a home drawing an average 1.5 kW lasts about 9 hours, and essentials alone at 0.5 kW last about 27 hours. With solar recharging during the day, many homes can run through multi-day outages if they trim heavy loads at night.

name: Enphase IQ Battery 5P
description: Enphase's modular 5kWh LFP battery that stacks in 5kWh steps, the natural pick for homes with Enphase microinverters that want to start small and grow.
quick: 5kWh LFP per unit, 3.84kW, Modular. Enphase's modular 5kWh LFP battery that stacks in 5kWh steps, the natural pick for homes with Enphase microinverters that want to start small and grow.
bestFor: Enphase solar homes that want to start small and add storage
skipIf: You want whole-home backup from one box
specs: AC-coupled; best with Enphase IQ microinverters
verdict: The IQ Battery 5P is the modular choice: buy as much storage as you need now and add more later. It fits best in homes that already run Enphase microinverters.

**Stacking is the point.** Each unit stores 5 kWh and is rated for 3.84 kW continuous and 7.68 kW of short-term peak. Two units give 10 kWh and 7.68 kW continuous; three give 15 kWh and about 11.5 kW, matching a [Powerwall 3](/gear/tesla-powerwall-3/) on power. At 3.84 kW, one unit covers a fridge, lights, internet and a gas furnace blower, but not central air.

**Runtime math.** One unit at a 0.5 kW essentials load lasts about 10 hours; three units at 1.5 kW also last about 10 hours. The [power station runtime calculator](/tools/power-station-runtime-calculator/) shows the same watt-hour math.

**AC-coupled and LFP.** Each battery has built-in microinverters, so it couples on the AC side and works with existing solar, but the cleanest setup is an all-Enphase system in one app. It uses [LFP](/glossary/lifepo4/) cells and carries a 15-year limited warranty. Backup needs Enphase's IQ System Controller to isolate the house from the grid.

Owners report easy app monitoring and like adding units over time; the common complaint is that cost per kWh climbs as you stack units. The newer [IQ Battery 10C](/gear/enphase-iq-battery-10c/) packs 10 kWh into one box. It ranks in our [home battery backup](/best-home-battery-backup/) guide.
pros: 3.84 kW continuous and 7.68 kW peak per unit
LFP cells with a 15-year limited warranty
One app for Enphase solar and storage
cons: One unit cannot start central air
Cost per kWh rises as you stack
Needs the IQ System Controller for backup

faqs.q: How many Enphase IQ Battery 5P units do you need?
faqs.a: For essentials, one or two. One unit gives 5 kWh and 3.84 kW, enough for a fridge, lights, internet and a furnace blower. Two give 10 kWh and 7.68 kW continuous. For whole-home backup with central air, plan on three or more, which reaches 15 kWh and about 11.5 kW continuous, similar to a single Powerwall 3.

faqs.q: IQ Battery 5P vs IQ Battery 10C: what is the difference?
faqs.a: The [10C](/gear/enphase-iq-battery-10c/) packs 10 kWh and 7.08 kVA continuous into one unit, while two 5P units give the same 10 kWh with 7.68 kW continuous. The 10C saves wall space and install labor. The 5P lets you buy in smaller steps. Both use LFP cells and carry 15-year limited warranties from Enphase.

name: FranklinWH aPower 2
description: FranklinWH's 15kWh LFP battery rated 10kW continuous, paired with an aGate controller that manages solar, grid and a backup generator from one box.
quick: 15kWh LFP, 10kW, aGate Controller. FranklinWH's 15kWh LFP battery rated 10kW continuous, paired with an aGate controller that manages solar, grid and a backup generator from one box.
bestFor: Battery-plus-generator backup managed from one box
skipIf: No certified FranklinWH installer serves your area
specs: AC-coupled; works with most existing solar
verdict: The aPower 2 is the most flexible of the installed batteries, and the best fit for rural homes that want a battery and a generator working together. It is sold through certified installers only.

**Capacity and power.** FranklinWH rates it at 15 kWh of usable storage and 10 kW of continuous output per unit. That is 1.5 kWh more storage than a [Powerwall 3](/gear/tesla-powerwall-3/), with slightly less continuous power. At 10 kW, about 42 amps at 240 volts, one unit runs most homes including a typical central AC. At an average 1.5 kW outage load, 15 kWh lasts about 10 hours.

**The aGate is the point.** The aGate controller sits between the battery, the grid, the house and any solar. It is designed to work with solar from other manufacturers and has a dedicated input for a standby or portable generator. When the battery runs low in a long outage, the generator can start and recharge it, managed from one box instead of improvised switching. See [transfer switch](/glossary/transfer-switch/) for how backup isolation works.
**Chemistry and warranty.** It uses [LFP](/glossary/lifepo4/) cells, and FranklinWH backs it with a 15-year warranty. Multiple units can share one aGate as needs grow.

Owners report smooth generator integration and good app control; the common complaint is a thinner installer network than Tesla or Enphase in some areas. Pair it with a standby like the [Generac Guardian 22kW](/gear/generac-guardian-22kw/) for long outages. It appears in our [home battery backup](/best-home-battery-backup/) guide.
pros: aGate has a dedicated generator input
cons: Installer-only, price set by local quote
Smaller installer network
Less continuous power than a Powerwall 3

faqs.q: Can the FranklinWH aPower 2 work with a generator?
faqs.a: Yes. The aGate controller has a dedicated generator input, so a standby or portable generator can start and recharge the battery when it runs low in a long outage. The aGate manages the handoff between grid, battery, solar and generator. Have your installer confirm your generator model and wiring are supported.

faqs.q: FranklinWH aPower 2 vs Tesla Powerwall 3: which is better?
faqs.a: The Powerwall 3 has more power, 11.5 kW versus 10 kW continuous, and a built-in solar inverter for new installs. The aPower 2 stores more, 15 kWh versus 13.5 kWh, and its aGate adds a generator input and works with existing solar. Pick Tesla for new solar, FranklinWH for generator pairing or retrofits.

name: Bluetti AC500 + B300S
amazon: Bluetti AC500 B300S power station battery
description: A plug-in modular system: a 5,000W 120V inverter head plus 3,072Wh LFP battery packs, expandable to about 18.4kWh, for gas-heated homes on city water.
quick: 5kW Inverter, 3.07kWh per B300S, 120V. A plug-in modular system: a 5,000W 120V inverter head plus 3,072Wh LFP battery packs, expandable to about 18.4kWh, for gas-heated homes on city water.
bestFor: Plug-in backup for gas-heated homes on city water
skipIf: You need 240V for a well pump or central air
verdict: The AC500 with B300S packs is the do-it-yourself alternative to an installed wall battery. It suits gas-heated homes on city water that want serious backup without an installer.

**Modular by design.** The AC500 is a 5,000 W inverter head with a 10,000 W surge rating, and it pairs with separate B300S battery packs of 3,072 Wh each. Bluetti allows up to six packs per AC500, about 18.4 kWh. Start with one or two and add more later. Each piece is lighter than a single giant unit, which helps on stairs.

**Runtime math.** Two packs hold 6,144 Wh. At a 500 W essentials load (fridge, lights, internet, furnace blower) that is roughly 10 to 11 hours after inverter losses; see the [power station runtime calculator](/tools/power-station-runtime-calculator/). The built-in solar input lets panels recharge it during the day, making it a [solar generator](/glossary/solar-generator/) in practice.

**The 120V limit.** The AC500 is a 120V system. It cannot run a 240V well pump, an electric dryer or central air on its own. Bluetti sells a separate box to combine two units for 240V output, but at that point an installed battery like the [Enphase IQ Battery 5P](/gear/enphase-iq-battery-5p/) is usually simpler. The packs use [LFP](/glossary/lifepo4/) cells for long cycle life.
Owners report it is easy to set up and expand; the common complaints are the weight of each pack and the 120V ceiling. It appears in our [home battery backup](/best-home-battery-backup/) guide.
pros: Expandable to about 18.4 kWh with six B300S packs
No installer or permit for plug-in use
cons: 120V only without a second unit and combiner box
Each B300S pack is heavy
Whole-house hookup still needs a transfer switch and electrician

faqs.q: Can the Bluetti AC500 run a refrigerator?
faqs.a: Yes, easily. A fridge averages about 100 to 200 watts and surges to roughly 1,200 to 2,000 watts at startup, well inside the 5,000 W continuous and 10,000 W surge ratings. One 3,072 Wh B300S pack runs a typical fridge alone for roughly 15 to 20 hours, and two packs add room for lights and internet.

faqs.q: Bluetti AC500 + B300S vs Tesla Powerwall 3: which is better?
faqs.a: They solve different problems. The [Powerwall 3](/gear/tesla-powerwall-3/) is installed, runs 240V loads at 11.5 kW continuous and stores 13.5 kWh. The AC500 is plug-in, 120V only at 5,000 W, and scales to about 18.4 kWh with six packs. Pick Bluetti for no-installer backup of essentials, Tesla for whole-home backup with central air.

name: Enphase IQ Battery 10C
description: Enphase's newer 10kWh LFP battery with 7.08kVA continuous output in a single unit, for Enphase solar homes that want more storage per box and fewer units to install.
quick: 10kWh LFP, 7.08kVA, all-in-one. Enphase's newer 10kWh LFP battery with 7.08kVA continuous output in a single unit, for Enphase solar homes that want more storage per box and fewer units to install.
bestFor: Enphase solar homes that want 10 kWh in one box
skipIf: You need more than 7 kW continuous from a single unit
specs: All-in-one battery with four grid-forming microinverters
verdict: The IQ Battery 10C is Enphase's answer to the criticism that its 5 kWh units take too many boxes. It packs 10 kWh into one battery and is the better Enphase buy for most new installs.

**Capacity and power.** Enphase rates it at 10 kWh of usable capacity and 7.08 kVA of continuous output from four embedded, grid-forming microinverters. At 240 volts, 7.08 kVA is about 29.5 amps. That runs a fridge, freezer, furnace, well pump, lights and internet, and can start some smaller central AC units; larger ones may need a soft starter or a second battery. At a 1 kW average outage load, 10 kWh lasts about 10 hours.

**Why it beats two 5Ps.** Two [IQ Battery 5P](/gear/enphase-iq-battery-5p/) units give the same 10 kWh with slightly more continuous power, 7.68 kW, but take two units to mount and wire. The 10C cuts that to one box. Enphase specifies 56 amps of peak current for three seconds for motor starts.

**Chemistry and warranty.** It uses [LFP](/glossary/lifepo4/) cells, and the limited warranty runs 15 years or 6,000 cycles. It is AC-coupled, so it works on the AC side of the system rather than through a hybrid inverter, and it is sold through Enphase installers.

Early owners report smooth app setup alongside Enphase solar; the main complaint is that 7.08 kVA trails the [Powerwall 3](/gear/tesla-powerwall-3/) at 11.5 kW. Compare it with the other installed batteries in our [home battery backup](/best-home-battery-backup/) guide.
cons: Less continuous power than a Powerwall 3
Installer-only
Large central AC units may need a soft starter or a second battery

faqs.q: Can the Enphase IQ Battery 10C run central air?
faqs.a: Sometimes. Its 7.08 kVA continuous rating is about 29.5 amps at 240 volts, enough to run many 2- to 3-ton AC units once started, and Enphase specifies 56 amps of peak current for three seconds for motor starts. Larger or older units may need a soft starter or a second battery. Your installer should check the AC's locked-rotor amps.

faqs.q: How long will an Enphase IQ Battery 10C last in an outage?
faqs.a: It holds 10 kWh usable. A home averaging 1 kW lasts about 10 hours, and essentials alone at 0.5 kW last about 20 hours. With Enphase solar recharging during the day, many homes can carry through multi-day outages if heavy loads wait until the sun is up.

name: Generac PWRcell 2
description: Generac's modular home battery, 9 to 36kWh in 3kWh steps and up to 11.5kW continuous, built to pair with a Generac standby generator for unlimited outage coverage.
quick: 9–36kWh modular, up to 11.5kW, Generac generator integration. Generac's modular home battery, 9 to 36kWh in 3kWh steps and up to 11.5kW continuous, built to pair with a Generac standby generator for unlimited outage coverage.
bestFor: Generac standby owners who want battery plus generator backup
skipIf: You want a single all-in-one box
specs: 9–18 kWh per cabinet in 3 kWh modules; up to 36 kWh
5.2–10.5 kW per cabinet; 11.5 kW max system
3 to 6 modules per cabinet; two cabinets per inverter
Modular cabinet system, integrates Generac standby up to 28 kW
AC-coupled; Generac PWRmicro or Enphase IQ8
verdict: PWRcell 2 is the battery to pick if you own, or plan to buy, a Generac standby generator. It is also the most granular system here, scaling from 9 to 36 kWh.

**Sized in 3 kWh steps.** Each cabinet takes three to six 3 kWh modules, for 9, 12, 15 or 18 kWh, and two cabinets can share one inverter for up to 36 kWh. Continuous power rises with module count: 5.2 kW with three modules, 10.5 kW with six, and 11.5 kW maximum with two cabinets. Generac lists AC start capacity of 65 to 130 amps by configuration, which decides whether it can start central air.

**The generator link is the point.** The Smart Disconnect Switch ties the grid, solar, battery and a Generac air-cooled standby up to 28 kW into one hub. The battery covers short outages silently, and the generator, such as a [Guardian 22kW](/gear/generac-guardian-22kw/), takes over in long ones, limited only by fuel. See [standby generator](/glossary/standby-generator/) for how those work.

**Solar and warranty.** The system is AC-coupled and works with Generac PWRmicro or Enphase IQ8 microinverters. Battery modules carry a 10-year or 7.56 MWh warranty, and round-trip efficiency is listed at 88%. All enclosures are NEMA 3R. At an average 1.5 kW outage load, 18 kWh lasts about 12 hours; the [runtime calculator](/tools/power-station-runtime-calculator/) works the same math.

Owners report that pairing it with a standby makes outages a non-event; the common complaint is a thinner installer base than Tesla. Compare it in our [home battery backup](/best-home-battery-backup/) guide.

Up to 11.5 kW continuous with two cabinets
Integrates Generac standby generators up to 28 kW

NEMA 3R enclosures for indoor or outdoor install

faqs.q: Does Generac PWRcell 2 work with a Generac standby generator?
faqs.a: Yes. Generac lists compatibility with its single-phase, air-cooled standby generators from 10 to 28 kW with an Evolution or Power Zone 200 controller. The Smart Disconnect Switch manages grid, solar, battery and generator, so the battery handles short outages and the generator takes over in long ones. Portable generators are excluded.

faqs.q: How many PWRcell 2 modules do you need?
faqs.a: For essentials, three or four modules: 9 to 12 kWh with 5.2 to 7 kW continuous. For whole-home backup with central air, six modules give 18 kWh, 10.5 kW and 130 amps of AC start capacity. Two cabinets reach 36 kWh and 11.5 kW. Ask your installer to size it against your AC's starting current.

name: LG RESU Prime 16H
description: LG's 16kWh high-voltage battery rated 7kW continuous and 11kW peak, a DC-coupled option for solar installs built around a compatible hybrid inverter.
quick: 16kWh high-voltage, 7kW continuous / 11kW peak. LG's 16kWh high-voltage battery rated 7kW continuous and 11kW peak, a DC-coupled option for solar installs built around a compatible hybrid inverter.
bestFor: Solar installs built around a compatible hybrid inverter
skipIf: You want an all-in-one battery with its own inverter
specs: DC-coupled through a compatible hybrid inverter
High-voltage DC battery, IP55, indoor or outdoor
Up to 2 in parallel (32 kWh, 14 kW)
verdict: The RESU Prime 16H is a big, simple battery for installers building around a compatible hybrid inverter. It is a solid choice when your solar installer already works with LG.

**Capacity first.** LG rates it at 16.0 kWh of usable energy, more than a [Powerwall 3](/gear/tesla-powerwall-3/) at 13.5 kWh. At an average outage load of 1.5 kW, that is nearly 11 hours; trimmed to essentials at 0.5 kW, about 32 hours. See [watt-hours](/glossary/watt-hours/) for how to read capacity.

**Power is the limit.** Continuous charge and discharge power is 7 kW, with 11 kW of peak for 10 seconds. At 240 volts, 7 kW is about 29 amps, enough for a fridge, freezer, furnace, well pump and lights, and possibly a smaller central AC if the 11 kW peak covers its start. Two units in parallel reach 32 kWh and 14 kW.

**It is half a system.** The 16H is a high-voltage DC battery, discharging at 350 to 410 volts, so it needs a compatible hybrid inverter to connect to solar and the house. That makes the inverter brand the deciding factor for features and backup switching. It weighs 350 lb, is rated IP55 for indoor or outdoor floor mounting, and carries a 10-year warranty.

Owners report quiet operation and a long-running product line; the common complaints are the weight and dependence on the inverter's software. Compare it with the units in our [home battery backup](/best-home-battery-backup/) guide, and run the numbers with the [runtime calculator](/tools/power-station-runtime-calculator/).

IP55, indoor or outdoor floor mount
cons: Needs a separate compatible hybrid inverter

faqs.q: Does the LG RESU Prime 16H need a special inverter?
faqs.a: Yes. It is a high-voltage DC battery that charges at 420 to 450 volts and discharges at 350 to 410 volts, so it must connect through a compatible hybrid inverter. It cannot plug into a standard grid-tied solar inverter or run household loads on its own. Your installer picks the inverter, which also handles backup switching.

faqs.q: LG RESU Prime 16H vs Tesla Powerwall 3: which is better?
faqs.a: The LG stores more, 16 kWh versus 13.5 kWh usable. The Powerwall 3 delivers far more power, 11.5 kW continuous versus 7 kW, and includes its own solar inverter. For whole-home backup with central air, the Powerwall is stronger. The LG suits installers who already use a compatible hybrid inverter and want maximum storage per unit.

name: SolarEdge Home Battery
description: SolarEdge's 9.7kWh DC-coupled battery rated 5kW continuous, the natural add-on for homes with a SolarEdge Home Hub inverter and optimizer-based solar.
quick: 9.7kWh, 5kW continuous, DC-coupled to SolarEdge. SolarEdge's 9.7kWh DC-coupled battery rated 5kW continuous, the natural add-on for homes with a SolarEdge Home Hub inverter and optimizer-based solar.
bestFor: Homes with a SolarEdge Home Hub inverter
skipIf: Your solar uses another inverter brand
specs: DC-coupled through a SolarEdge Home Hub inverter
400V DC battery for SolarEdge Home Hub systems
verdict: The SolarEdge Home Battery makes sense mainly for one buyer: a home with, or planning, a SolarEdge solar system. Inside that ecosystem it is a clean, efficient fit.

**Capacity and power.** SolarEdge lists 9.7 kWh of storage and 5 kW of continuous power, with a 7.5 kW maximum rating. At 240 volts, 5 kW is about 21 amps. That covers a fridge, freezer, gas furnace blower, sump pump, lights and internet, but not central air on its own. At a 0.5 kW essentials load, 9.7 kWh lasts about 19 hours.

**DC coupling is the point.** It is a 400V battery that connects on the DC side of a SolarEdge Home Hub inverter, so solar can charge it without an extra conversion step. That is efficient, but it also means it does not suit homes with other inverter brands. Backup also needs SolarEdge's backup interface, which isolates the house from the grid like a [transfer switch](/glossary/transfer-switch/).
**Build and warranty.** It weighs about 262 lb (119 kg) and carries a 10-year warranty. Several batteries can share one inverter for more storage.

Owners report seamless monitoring in the SolarEdge app; the common complaints are the ecosystem lock-in and modest power next to a [Powerwall 3](/gear/tesla-powerwall-3/) or [FranklinWH aPower 2](/gear/franklinwh-apower-2/). See our [home battery backup](/best-home-battery-backup/) guide for how it compares.
cons: Works only with SolarEdge inverters
Cannot run central air alone

faqs.q: Does the SolarEdge Home Battery work with other solar inverters?
faqs.a: No. It is a 400V DC-coupled battery designed for SolarEdge Home Hub inverters, and it connects on the inverter's DC side. Homes with Enphase microinverters or other string inverters need a different battery, such as an AC-coupled Enphase IQ Battery or a FranklinWH aPower 2. Check your inverter model before you get quotes.

faqs.q: How long will a SolarEdge Home Battery run a house?
faqs.a: With 9.7 kWh of storage, a home averaging 1 kW lasts about 9.7 hours and essentials at 0.5 kW last about 19 hours. Its 5 kW continuous rating caps what can run at once, so central air is usually off the list. Solar recharging during the day stretches backup across longer outages.

name: Tesla Powerwall 2
description: Tesla's earlier 13.5kWh home battery rated 5kW continuous, still on many homes and in some quotes; know its power limits before you count on it for central air.
quick: 13.5kWh NMC, 5kW continuous / 7kW peak (legacy). Tesla's earlier 13.5kWh home battery rated 5kW continuous, still on many homes and in some quotes; know its power limits before you count on it for central air.
bestFor: Understanding an existing install or a discounted retrofit quote
skipIf: You need central air from a single battery
specs: AC-coupled battery with Backup Gateway (legacy model)
AC-coupled; works with existing solar inverters
verdict: The Powerwall 2 is no longer Tesla's current battery, but it is still on many homes and in some installer quotes, so it is worth knowing what it can and cannot do. If you are buying new, compare it closely with the [Powerwall 3](/gear/tesla-powerwall-3/).

**Same capacity, less power.** Tesla rates it at 13.5 kWh of usable energy, the same as the Powerwall 3, but only 5 kW continuous and 7 kW peak for 10 seconds. At 240 volts, 5 kW is about 21 amps. One unit runs a fridge, freezer, furnace blower, lights and internet comfortably, but central air usually needs two units or a soft starter.

**AC-coupled.** It works with existing solar inverters on the AC side, through Tesla's Backup Gateway, which isolates the house from the grid in an outage. That made it the go-to retrofit battery for homes that already had solar. It uses lithium-ion [NMC](/glossary/nmc-battery/) cells rather than the [LFP](/glossary/lifepo4/) chemistry in the Powerwall 3.
**Weight and warranty.** It weighs 251 lb (units built after March 2019) and carries a 10-year warranty that requires an internet connection. At a 1 kW average load, 13.5 kWh lasts about 13.5 hours.

Owners of existing systems report reliable backup and a good app; the common complaint is that 5 kW per unit limits what can run at once. Compare current options in our [home battery backup](/best-home-battery-backup/) guide.
pros: Proven on a large installed base
cons: 5 kW continuous, less than half a Powerwall 3
NMC rather than LFP chemistry
Superseded by the Powerwall 3

faqs.q: What is the difference between Powerwall 2 and Powerwall 3?
faqs.a: Both store 13.5 kWh usable. The Powerwall 3 delivers 11.5 kW continuous versus 5 kW, uses LFP instead of NMC cells, and has a built-in solar inverter, while the Powerwall 2 is AC-coupled and pairs with an existing inverter. For whole-home backup with central air, one Powerwall 3 does what typically took two Powerwall 2 units.

faqs.q: Can a Tesla Powerwall 2 run central air?
faqs.a: Usually not alone. Its 5 kW continuous and 7 kW peak ratings are tight for a central AC's starting surge. Two Powerwall 2 units, at 10 kW continuous combined, or a soft starter on the compressor are the common fixes. Your installer can check the AC's locked-rotor amps against the battery before you count on it.
